rounds.proof_sketch: The mutation is in the float16 (half) template specialization at line 24. For float32 inputs (dtype=torch.float32 as specified), AT_DISPATCH_FLOATING_TYPES_AND_HALF instantiates the generic template<typename T> kernel at lines 12-18, which was NOT mutated. The mutated half specialization (lines 20-26) is only invoked when input.scalar_type() is Half/float16. Since dtype=torch.float32 is fixed in the input specification, the mutated code path is never executed.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutant survives because the mutation only affects the half-precision (float16) template specialization of the softsign kernel, changing the boundary check from 'idx < size' to 'idx < size - 1'. However, the fixed input specification mandates dtype=torch.float32, which causes AT_DISPATCH_FLOATING_TYPES_AND_HALF to instantiate the generic (unmutated) template rather than the mutated half specialization. The Dtype Stress tests that supposedly tested float16 may have failed to properly exercise this code path or used a different comparison method. Under the strict fixed-shape/fixed-dtype contract where dtype=torch.float32 cannot be changed, the mutated code is effectively dead code that can never be reached.
rounds.kill_strategy: Unkillable under fixed dtype=torch.float32 contract. The mutation only affects float16 inputs. To kill this mutant would require changing dtype to torch.float16, which violates the input specification constraint. If dtype were changeable, using float16 with any non-garbage value at the last element position would expose the bug since the mutant leaves output[-1,-1] uninitialized.
rounds.recommendations: When designing mutation tests for kernels with dtype-specific template specializations, ensure the test suite exercises ALL dtype paths that the kernel supports, not just the dtype specified in default inputs. Consider adding explicit dtype coverage requirements to the testing contract, or restructure the kernel to avoid having untested dtype-specific code paths. Additionally, mutation testing frameworks should flag mutations in dtype-specific code paths that aren't covered by the current input specification.
